headLandmarks.name: glabella
headLandmarks.definition: The most anterior point on the frontal bone midway between the bony browridges.
headLandmarks.citation: Hotzman et al. 2011, NATICK/TR-11/017, 5.2.14, p. 36
headLandmarks.rule: largest z among head midline vertices (hm08.mirror 'm') whose neutral height lies within the eyebrow card's neutral vertical extent; the card's extent stands in for the browridge height
headLandmarks.limit: The vertex is fixed on the neutral head. When the shape changes, the definition's extremum can move to another vertex, and a fixed vertex does not follow that move.
headLandmarks.convention: View vertices index the head view's skin surface 0 (the face's `Human`); `vertex` and loop rows are generation skin samples (base-mesh vertices keep their index). Positions are neutral metres in the right-handed Y-up, Z-forward frame the face and body share, so +X is the anatomical left; a sided name is the anatomical side.

headLandmarks.name: sellion
headLandmarks.definition: The point of the deepest depression of the nasal bones at the top of the nose.
headLandmarks.citation: Hotzman et al. 2011, NATICK/TR-11/017, 5.2.35, p. 59
headLandmarks.rule: smallest z on the outer midline profile from glabella to pronasale, end points excluded; the profile is the shortest path over base-mesh midline edges (hm08.mirror 'm'), and pronasale is the most anterior midline vertex above the mouth joint
headLandmarks.limit: The vertex is fixed on the neutral head. When the shape changes, the definition's extremum can move to another vertex, and a fixed vertex does not follow that move.
headLandmarks.convention: View vertices index the head view's skin surface 0 (the face's `Human`); `vertex` and loop rows are generation skin samples (base-mesh vertices keep their index). Positions are neutral metres in the right-handed Y-up, Z-forward frame the face and body share, so +X is the anatomical left; a sided name is the anatomical side.

headLandmarks.name: menton
headLandmarks.definition: The inferior point of the mandible in the midsagittal plane (bottom of the chin).
headLandmarks.citation: Hotzman et al. 2011, NATICK/TR-11/017, 5.2.23, p. 45
headLandmarks.rule: lowest head midline vertex whose jaw attachment weight is one within storage, with the jaw closed; skin that moves entirely with the mandible stands in for the mandible, because the midline profile keeps descending from the chin into the neck
headLandmarks.limit: The vertex is fixed on the neutral head. When the shape changes, the definition's extremum can move to another vertex, and a fixed vertex does not follow that move.
headLandmarks.convention: View vertices index the head view's skin surface 0 (the face's `Human`); `vertex` and loop rows are generation skin samples (base-mesh vertices keep their index). headLandmarks.citation: Farkas 1994; same point as menton (ANSUR II 5.2.23)
headLandmarks.rule: same vertex as menton (same point as menton, ANSUR II 5.2.23): the Farkas gnathion and the ANSUR menton name one skin point
headLandmarks.limit: The vertex is fixed on the neutral head. When the shape changes, the definition's extremum can move to another vertex, and a fixed vertex does not follow that move.
headLandmarks.convention: View vertices index the head view's skin surface 0 (the face's `Human`); `vertex` and loop rows are generation skin samples (base-mesh vertices keep their index). headLandmarks.name: tragion-right
headLandmarks.definition: The superior point on the juncture of the cartilaginous flap (tragus) of the ear with the head.
headLandmarks.citation: Hotzman et al. 2011, NATICK/TR-11/017, 5.2.42, p. 66
headLandmarks.rule: uppermost vertex of the anterior tragus–head juncture, chosen by reading rendered frames of the neutral right ear (frame path); the compared neighbours and the reading ambiguity of about 0.4 mm are listed with the candidates
headLandmarks.limit: The vertex is fixed on the neutral head. When the shape changes, the definition's extremum can move to another vertex, and a fixed vertex does not follow that move.
headLandmarks.ambiguity: Within 0.4 mm the reading cannot separate the chosen vertex from the compared neighbours 5699, 5610 (nearest first); read on: right ear of the neutral generation person: side, front and three-quarter, normal and clay, candidates marked.
headLandmarks.convention: View vertices index the head view's skin surface 0 (the face's `Human`); `vertex` and loop rows are generation skin samples (base-mesh vertices keep their index). Positions are neutral metres in the right-handed Y-up, Z-forward frame the face and body share, so +X is the anatomical left; a sided name is the anatomical side.

headLandmarks.name: subnasale

headLandmarks.citation: Katina et al. 2016, J Anat, Table 2
headLandmarks.rule: corner where the midline profile turns from the columella slope into the upper lip, read on rendered frames of the neutral nose (frame path)
headLandmarks.limit: The vertex is fixed on the neutral head. When the shape changes, the definition's extremum can move to another vertex, and a fixed vertex does not follow that move.
headLandmarks.ambiguity: Within 2.3 mm the reading cannot separate the chosen vertex from the compared neighbours 5072, 317 (nearest first); read on: neutral person nose, side clay with midline candidates marked.
headLandmarks.convention: View vertices index the head view's skin surface 0 (the face's `Human`); `vertex` and loop rows are generation skin samples (base-mesh vertices keep their index). Positions are neutral metres in the right-handed Y-up, Z-forward frame the face and body share, so +X is the anatomical left; a sided name is the anatomical side.

teeth.convention: Region rows are vertex IDs of the face's `Human.teeth_base` surface; centroids are neutral head-frame metres (right-handed Y-up, Z-forward, +X the anatomical left); tooth codes follow ISO 3950 with the anatomical sides.
teeth.rule: 32 components of 63 vertices; upper/lower within each mutual nearest antagonist pair in the horizontal plane, the higher centroid being upper; right/left by the sign of x; within a quadrant ordered from the midline by the centroid angle about the mean centroid, measured from +Z; ISO 3950 quadrants 1 upper right, 2 upper left, 3 lower left, 4 lower right
teeth.gingivaAndPalate: not separated in the CC0 mesh; not written (absent registration)

marginChain.rule: anchors = 2 mm station pairs and the central contact pair; stops = negative join, anchors by along, positive join; consecutive stops joined by the shortest 3D path over the component's lips triangles within the limit; first occurrences kept

periocular.convention: Margin rows index the face skin surface `Human` (the head view's surface 0); brow, lash and globe rows index their own named surfaces; optical rows are native `Human.low-poly` vertex IDs. Positions, axes and the reference are neutral head-frame metres and unit vectors in the right-handed Y-up, Z-forward frame, so +X is the anatomical left; left and right are anatomical sides, never read from asset names.

margins.source: HUMAN_SOURCE_READ_MARGINS (left, base mesh vertices; right = mirror twins in the same order)
margins.frames: neutral person eyes, front clay and normal with margin candidates marked

brows.rule: split by the sign of x (+X left)

lashes.rule: split by the sign of x (+X left)

canthi.rule: extreme of the joined margin rows on the head-frame x axis; left eye medial minimum and lateral maximum, right eye reversed
canthi.limit: The canthus is the x-axis extreme of the joined registered margin rows on the final skin, so it follows an edit that moves which row vertex is the corner; a corner moved beyond the registered rows is not found, and the head-frame x axis stands in for the palpebral fissure axis.

opticalSupport.rule: axis from joint-l-eye toward joint-l-eye-target; origin joint-l-eye; anterior = the one facing component triangle the axis line meets

fieldProducers.method: lean muscular body minus lean average-muscle body built through the body view, along symmetric area-weighted normals; band-passed by uniform-Laplacian sweeps f <- (f + neighbour mean)/2 (high sweeps less low sweeps), gain, made bilaterally symmetric; smoothstep fade within the fade length of the nipple-areola centres (skin landmark nipple-left and its mirror twin) and the crotch cut; zero on the support of each relief endpoint with the same smoothstep fade outward (each owns its muscle's relief); split over the breast mound by the cupsize endpoint's normalized length smoothed by the high sweeps; along the normals only; nipple region refilled; stored at 10 micrometres
fieldProducers.kept: input difference, sweep smoother and counts, gain, smoothstep fade length, symmetry: checked against the r6 receipt's arithmetic on the r5 surface (rms 0.016 mm away from the regions the receipt leaves undetermined)

chosen.reliefStepAside: zero on the support of each relief endpoint, smoothstep fade over the fade length outward; the receipt's 'stepping aside' does not determine a rule, and the endpoint that owns a muscle's relief should carry it alone
chosen.breastSplit: weight is the cupsize-max endpoint's length over its maximum, smoothed by the high sweeps and clamped to [0, 1]; chest and musculature come from the same run
chosen.nippleCentres: the body view's nipple-left skin landmark and its mirror twin, replacing the r6 coordinates recovered from that revision's neutral

fieldProducers.method: per extended side: endpoint motion = implicit heat diffusion of the endpoint vector over the motion length; residual thickness along symmetric area-weighted normals; detail = thickness less its diffusion over the thickness length; corrective row = -(end - node) * detail * normal, ramped from the node to the end; mirror-averaged; nipple region refilled; stored at 10 micrometres
fieldProducers.kept: structure, cotangent Laplacian with lumped mass, diffusion lengths 150 and 40 mm, each side's end (envelope-detail-receipt.json)

chosen.stepLength: t = L^2 / 2, the heat kernel's variance 2t equal to a Gaussian's sigma^2 with sigma = L
chosen.heldBoundary: Dirichlet: open-boundary vertices keep their input value
chosen.surface: the body view's neutral and symmetric normals
chosen.symmetry: mirror average of the corrective rows
chosen.detailFraction: this run's reading is rms detail over rms thickness on the endpoint's support; the receipt's own definition is not recorded, so the two are listed side by side and not fitted

fieldProducers.method: repository contact solver (createBodyCorrectiveSession) on the body view without the dropped correctives, merged with exact mirrors at 10 micrometres (mergeBodyCorrectives)
fieldProducers.solverChange: the published round-9 correctives came from an earlier solver; the current one bisects the onset over the whole shape, prices pushes by per-pair tissue budgets and queues a still-crossing ramp midpoint as its own state, so the same state yields its own correctives

records.outcome: repaired; the midpoint of the joint ramp still crosses and is queued
